name: A mass on a spring
description:
A mass on a spring, x'' = −ω²·x − 2ζω·x', written as two compartments, the position x and the velocity v, whose dy/dt terms read each other. Both swing through zero, so "cannot go negative" is off on each. With no damping (zeta = 0) the mass swings between x = ±1 once a second for ever, and its energy (v² + ω²x²)/2 never changes. Exact is the closed form, which holds for any damping ratio below 1.

Twenty periods are long enough for a solver's phase error to show. At the same relative tolerance of 1e-8, dp45 ends 1.2e-7 from Exact after 1682 steps, and the seventh-order vern7 ends 1.6e-9 away after 562. The NDF solver, made for stiff decay rather than for oscillation, ends 6e-6 away and has lost 1.2e-5 of the energy: its damping is numerical, not physical.

Try: zeta = 0.1 for a damped oscillator, then switch solvers and compare x with Exact.
